shots.picture: Moonlit street, DP framing: the Piper playing in front; behind him a procession of children 3 abreast, perfect lockstep. Every head snaps to camera on the plucked "ta-ta"
shots.music: Taunt hook A5 F#5 B5 A5 F#5 at 0.000; pluck answer 0.882 / 0.993

shots.picture: Extreme close-up: his fingers on the recorder (real fingering of each note)
shots.music: Bar 2 flute call (Bm->C, the F# tritone rub)

shots.picture: Close-up under the hat brim: his eyes open, glowing
Low and tight: children's legs and hems crossing in lockstep, heels on the beats
From above: the procession winds through the moonlit town, three abreast, still growing
Day, sepia (Hamelin, 1284): rats flood the square from the stall, drain and well; villagers leap on the claps
Rats gallop along the roof ridges, leaping the gaps
Grain sacks burst one by one (s8 / s10 / s13); the merchant recoils
A family kitchen: rats run across the table; the mother leaps onto the bench (clap), the father raises a stool (clap), the boy hides, the cat backs away
A barrel lid flies off; rats burst out in three waves (s0 / s3 / s6)
From above: the street is a carpet of 240 rats; townsfolk flee against the flow
The town gate grinds open (the ratchet); townsfolk turn on the beats; a backlit silhouette; he steps through in the silence
Tracking backward: the stranger strides toward us through the market; villagers turn to him in a wave on the beats; rats scatter
Council chamber: palm up on the gurdy call, a sweep to the window (the rats), the recorder tapped on his answer; the council leans in
The chest of gold opens on the downbeat; the handshake on his answer; he bows and tips his hat
shots.music: Gurdy call / flute answer over C

shots.picture: Low angle: he raises the flute; wind; the rising run
shots.music: Spell: F#5 G5 A#5 B5 C#6 D6

shots.picture: Rat level: they scurry, freeze on the trill, turn their heads, and rise onto their hind legs in the silence
DROP 1: tracking beside him; behind him 140 rats in lockstep rows, tails swinging together; a hop ripples through the rows on the 16th scurry
Overhead: five counter-rotating rings pulse on the kick; the scurry ripples outward ring by ring
Rat's-eye: paws and tails pass the lens in lockstep; his legs stride behind
Along the wall: each rising plucked note lifts the next line of rats
Dusk, wide: a living ribbon of rats winds out of the gate down to the Weser behind him
They leap from the bank in arcs, two per 16th; only rings remain; he plays on his rock
The hit: one last ring; still water and his reflection
The whole town springs up into the DP squat dance (rows in canon), bunting, confetti
Closer: spins, stomps, jigs; the front rows clap on every beat
He walks through the dancers to the officials' table, his palm held out
The chest SLAMS shut on the betrayal downbeat (coins, dust); the mayor wags "no" in half time; his hand stays out
The town keeps dancing in half time with frozen grins around the perfectly still Piper; the officials laugh silently
Close-up: his smile dies; the sun sets across his face, the moon rises; on the C# hang he turns to us, eyes glowing
Night: his silhouette in the empty moonlit street raises the flute; a long moon shadow
A boy stops playing; the wooden horse falls from his hand
A candle flame bends toward the window; a girl's eyes open
Shutters burst open in a cascade; in the silence every window dims at once
DROP 2: doors fly open on the beats; children step out in matching strides toward the Piper
A forest of legs in lockstep, hems swinging, moon shadows
He walks toward us playing; rows of six behind him; children slide in from both sides on every 16th
Close faces: heads tilt in a canon on the cadence notes; in the break they snap to camera and freeze
From above: the procession snakes four abreast through the moonlit roofs, long shadows
Quarter-bar call and response: Piper against the moon / the crowd lifts its arms / Piper close / a row of heads tilts together
Silhouettes against a huge moon, climbing toward the mountain
The reveal: the whole procession winds across the valley into the glowing passage; it flares on the stab
At the passage: four stabs, four groups gone into the light; the last girl looks back; he steps in; the rock seals in the silence
The sealed mountain: footprints into solid rock, one small shoe, his feather falling
A mother with a candle finds the empty bed; the wooden horse on the floor
Dawn: parents in the empty doorways turn toward the mountain on the heartbeat; toys on the steps
The opening street, deserted: fog, the torch, a wooden horse
The horse rolls by itself on each giggle note; for a moment he is playing in the fog; the frame settles exactly on the opening composition
shots.music: Last giggle; F#5-G5 pickup loops into bar 1

captions.text: THE TOWN WAS OVERRUN BY RATS.
A STRANGER OFFERED TO SAVE THEM.
BUT THEY REFUSED TO PAY HIM.
